Are you an experienced hedge accounting professional looking for an opportunity to influence how hedge accounting is applied across one of the Nordic region's largest banks?
As a Hedge Accounting Specialist, you will play a key role in ensuring that Swedbank’s hedge accounting framework supports both regulatory requirements and the bank’s risk management objectives. You will work closely with colleagues across Treasury, Finance, Risk and Markets and contribute to the continued development of how hedge accounting is applied across the Group.
We recognise that few candidates will match every single one of the qualifications listed below. If you have solid hedge accounting expertise and are excited about the role, we encourage you to apply.
In Swedbank you have the opportunity to:
Shape and develop hedge accounting methodologies and frameworks:

Develop, analyse and maintain hedge accounting methodologies, frameworks and practices for Swedbank's Treasury activities.

Ensure compliance with IAS 39 and IFRS 9 while aligning accounting solutions with the bank's risk management strategies.

Contribute to the development of policies, processes and controls, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and quality.

Provide specialist advice and technical expertise:

Act as a subject matter expert on hedge accounting related to Treasury transactions, financial instruments and hedging strategies.

Analyse and resolve complex hedge accounting questions, translating technical requirements into practical solutions.

Monitor developments in IFRS and market practice and assess their impact on the bank. 

Collaborate and influence across the organisation:

Work closely with stakeholders across Treasury, Finance, Risk and Markets to ensure alignment between risk management and financial reporting.

Share your expertise and help strengthen hedge accounting capabilities across the organisation.

What is needed in this role:
Education and professional background:

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics or a related field.

Experience from a large bank, financial institution and/or audit firm is highly valued.  

Technical expertise: We are looking for expertise in hedge accounting and practical experience in several of the following areas:

IAS 39 and IFRS 9.

Hedge designation, documentation and effectiveness assessment.

Financial instruments and derivatives.

The interaction between accounting and financial risk management.  

Analytical and problem-solving skills:

Experience analysing and resolving complex hedge accounting matters.

Ability to interpret accounting standards and translate requirements into practical, sustainable solutions.

Strong analytical skills and a structured approach to complex topics.  

Collaboration and communication:

Ability to build relationships and collaborate across different functions.

Ability to build effective working relationships with a range of stakeholders.

Ability to explain complex topics clearly to both specialist and non-specialist audiences.

A collaborative, pragmatic and solution-oriented mindset.

Full professional proficiency in English is required, Swedish language skills are a plus.

Familiarity with general Treasury activities such as balance sheet management, interest rate risk- and FX risk management would be beneficial.

With us, you can experience:
Personal and professional growth through self-leadership and continuous development.

Meaningful work that positively impacts our workplace, our customers, and society.

An open and collaborative culture that encourages cross-functional teamwork and provides networking opportunities.

A supportive and inclusive environment that promotes a balanced and sustainable work-life, with flexible working conditions when suitable for the role.

Enjoy country-specific benefits, including banking offers, a pension plan, our share-based reward program, health insurance in the Baltics and a health allowance in Sweden.

"Join our team and...
... become part of a professional and collaborative Group Treasury organisation where your expertise will have a meaningful impact. You will work closely with experienced colleagues across Treasury, Finance and Risk, contributing to the continued development of Swedbank’s hedge accounting capabilities and financial risk management. This is an opportunity to take ownership of and influence how hedge accounting is applied and developed across Swedbank.”
Joakim Wande Hägge , your future manager 
We look forward to receiving your application by 03.01.2027. 
We will review applications continuously, which means that the position may be filled before the application deadline. Therefore, the job posting may be removed prior to the stated closing date.
Location: Stockholm, Sundbyberg
Recruiting manager: Joakim Wande Hägge 
We would like to let you know that a background check and a drug test may be a part of the process for this role.

Swedbank does not discriminate anybody based on gender, age, sexual orientation or sexual identity, ethnicity, religion or disability – everybody is welcome.

The role - People & Culture Coordinator (part-time student role)
Are you studying HR, psychology, business or a related field and looking for an opportunity to put what you're learning into practice alongside your studies?
As our People & Culture Coordinator, you'll gain hands-on experience across a variety of HR activities, working closely with our Head of People & Culture and the wider team. You'll be a friendly and approachable first point of contact for our MAGnificent colleagues, supporting them with everyday people-related questions and helping to keep our HR operations running smoothly.
You'll also have the opportunity to get involved in some exciting projects, including the implementation of our new HR system, where you can help shape and improve our ways of working. You'll work alongside our Office Coordinator to plan and organise employee events, helping to bring our colleagues together and contribute to our fun and inclusive workplace culture.
We don't expect you to know everything already! What's important to us is that you're curious, enjoy helping others and are keen to learn, take initiative and find solutions.
Working alongside your studies
This is a 12-month fixed-term position working 16 hours per week, with your hours spread across two or three days in our Stockholm office. We understand the importance of balancing work with your studies and are happy to discuss a working schedule that works for both you and the team.
The People & Culture team
We're a small, friendly and collaborative team working across our Stockholm and Brighton studios. Led by our Head of People & Culture, our team includes an Office Coordinator in each studio and our Talent Acquisition Manager.
We work closely together to create a positive employee experience across MAG, and we're looking forward to welcoming someone who can bring fresh ideas and perspectives to our team.
What you’ll be doing
Being a friendly first point of contact for employees with everyday HR questions.

Supporting the onboarding of new colleagues, from initial preparations to helping create a welcoming first-day experience.

Helping with the implementation of our new HR system, maintaining accurate employee information and supporting colleagues in using it.

Helping to coordinate employee surveys, wellbeing activities and diversity and inclusion initiatives.

Working alongside our Office Coordinator to plan and organise employee events.

Supporting employee relocations in collaboration with our relocation partner.

Exploring how technology and AI can help us improve our processes and ways of working.

Getting involved in other People & Culture projects, with opportunities to explore areas that particularly interest you.

Your skills/experience
You're currently studying HR, psychology, business administration or a related subject, having completed at least one year of your studies and with at least one year remaining.

You're based in the Stockholm area and available to work 16 hours per week from our office.

You're comfortable communicating in both Swedish and English, verbally and in writing.

You're organised, reliable and take pride in the quality and accuracy of your work.

You enjoy helping others, building relationships and interacting with colleagues across the company.

You're curious and resourceful, with the initiative to explore solutions and figure things out.

You understand the importance of confidentiality and can be trusted to handle sensitive information with care and discretion.

Nice to have (but not essential)
Previous experience in administration, reception, customer service or another people-focused role.

An interest in digital tools, AI and how technology can support HR activities.

What you'll gain
Practical HR experience across a broad range of People & Culture activities.

The opportunity to take ownership of your work, with responsibilities that grow as your experience and confidence develop.

Support and guidance from an experienced People & Culture team.

A flexible role that complements your studies.

The experience of working in a creative, friendly and international games company.

Perks and Benefits
Company mobile phone and contract

1:1 Mentor

Flexible working hours

Seasonal kick-off events

Gym allowance

Monthly after-work socials

Company-wide carbon offsetting and CSR initiatives

At MAG, we want all of our employees to feel valued, appreciated and empowered to bring their true selves to work!

TRATON is a group of strong brands with a shared mission: transforming transportation together to create the future of sustainable transport solutions. Within TRATON, we include MAN, Scania, Volkswagen Truck & Bus, and International. As part of a global team of industry experts, you get to think bigger, experience more, and reach further. Together, we have the power to transform transportation - Let´s make a difference together. Find out more: www.traton.com 
 
Our values – customer first, respect, team spirit, responsibility, and elimination of waste – are at the heart of everything we do. 
Role Summary
 
This role is a part of TRATON Group R&D, located in Södertälje, Sweden
 
Join Advanced Analytics and AI Solutions within VCF Vehicle Service Information to develop AI services and data products for the service market and workshops. You will work across the ML lifecycle, from data preparation, modelling and testing to deployment, monitoring and continuous improvement in operational use.
 
Job Responsibilities
 
Translate service market and workshop needs into clearly defined data science opportunities and measurable success criteria.
Prepare data and develop and validate statistical models, machine learning models and AI solutions.
Write maintainable, reusable and well tested production code using AWS and Snowflake, applying AI assisted development responsibly.
Deploy and operate solutions with engineers and platform colleagues, monitoring performance, data quality and work with continuous improvements.
Communicate results, model behaviour, uncertainty and limitations clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

 
Who You Are
 
You are an experienced Data Scientist with strong Python, SQL, statistics and machine learning skills. You work independently and collaboratively, communicate clearly in English, and have a relevant university degree.
 
You develop reproducible solutions using version control, testing and sound software practices. You have experience with AWS, Snowflake and familiarity in deployment, model serving, monitoring or MLOps.
 
You use Codex, Claude or similar AI assistants to speed up development and improve code, tests, documentation and analysis. You validate AI generated output through engineering judgement, testing, security checks and review.
 
Experience with generative AI, LLM or retrieval based services, and tools for orchestration, evaluation, observability and feedback driven improvement is an advantage.
 
We welcome applicants from all backgrounds – your unique experience and perspectives is valuable to us. 
This Is Us
 
Advanced Analytics and AI Solutions takes ideas from early exploration into practical use for service information, diagnostics and workshop processes. We collaborate with domain experts, product teams, engineers, platform colleagues and with the commercial side to improve the customer experience.
 
Our work spans Generative AI & LLMs, Predictive Maintenance & Diagnostics, Computer Vision, Advanced Analytics, and DataOps & MLOps.
 
Depending on the use case, we use Amazon Bedrock, Sagemaker, TensorFlow / PyTorch, ML flow, LangGraph, LangChain, DSPy and Langfuse to build, evaluate, monitor and improve AI services.
 
Within TRATON Group R&D, you are an important part of something bigger. Joining us means gaining access to the ins and outs of the entire transportation industry.  
TRATON Offers
 
We offer a dynamic and engaging workplace where collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement are part of everyday life. You will be part of a strong team environment that encourages knowledge sharing and close cooperation across functions.
 
With a structured development plan and a wide range of training opportunities, TRATON Group R&D supports your professional growth both locally and internationally.
 
Benefits include access to our health center in Gröndal or a wellness allowance, bonus, flexible working hours, and company car leasing. We also arrange events for employees and their families, and for those living in Stockholm, convenient commuting is supported through direct Scania Job express buses to Södertälje.
Application

Apply as soon as possible, no later than 2026-12-07. Screening will take place on an ongoing basis during the application period. Logical and personality tests may be used as part of the selection process, and a background check may be required for this role.

Orkla House Care is a leading provider of brushes, rollers and other painting tools, including consumables such as tape, sanding products, protection and cleaning equipment. The company is 100% owend by Orkla ASA and operates across the Nordic countries, the UK and Benelux, with strong brands such as Jordan, Harris, Anza, Spekter and Hamilton. Sales are primarily through paint shops and trade merchants. With around 670 employees and annual sales of approximately NOK 1.6 billion, Orkla House Care combines strong brands, in-house production and deep category expertise. Production takes place in Sweden, the UK and China, with the head office located at Skøyen in Oslo.
We are looking for a Category Manager Raw Material to join our Group Procurement team. In this role, you will own selected raw material categories (Packaging and Fabrics) across Orkla House Care, driving supplier performance, cost competitiveness, sustainability initiatives, and supply security.
You will play a key role in shaping the future direction of your categories. We are further developing our category management capabilities and are looking for someone who wants to be part of that journey. The role offers the opportunity to build category insights, define strategic priorities, identify value creation opportunities, and establish category roadmaps that support future growth.

Working closely with colleagues across Procurement, R&D, ESG/Sustainability, Quality, and Operations, you will translate category strategies into tangible business outcomes. You will have exposure across the organization and the opportunity to influence decisions, priorities, and value creation for Orkla House Care.
The role reports to the Head of Raw Material, Global Procurement and can be based in either Bromsgrove, UK or Bankeryd, Sweden, where Orkla House Care has offices and production sites.
Your key priorities will be:
Develop and execute category and sourcing strategies that drive cost competitiveness, supply security, quality performance, and long-term value creation.
Lead sourcing activities including supplier selection, RFQs, benchmarking, negotiations, and contract management.
Build and develop strategic supplier partnerships to drive innovation, continuous improvement, and sustainable business practices.
Manage supplier performance across cost, quality, delivery, compliance, and sustainability requirements.
Identify and deliver cost improvement initiatives while managing supply risks and ensuring business continuity.
Support product development, investment projects, and cross-functional initiatives in close collaboration with Procurement, R&D, Quality, and Operations.
Utilize procurement data, analytics, and digital tools to support fact-based decision-making and reporting

Qualifications
We believe you bring:
3+ years of experience within strategic procurement, category management or strategic sourcing, preferably from an international manufacturing environment.
Experience developing category strategies and leading sourcing and supplier initiatives that create measurable business value.
Strong capabilities in stakeholder management, supplier negotiations and cross-functional collaboration.
A commercial and data-driven approach to identifying opportunities and driving results.
Understanding of sustainability, responsible sourcing, and supplier compliance requirements.
A Bachelor's degree or equivalent within Business, Procurement, Supply Chain Management or a related field.
Fluency in English, written and spoken.

You identify with Orkla House Care’s values: Passion, Results, Integrity, Diversity and Empowerment.
Additional Information
Painting Our Future Together: At Orkla House Care, we believe the best results are created together. We are looking for people who take ownership, collaborate across teams and markets, and contribute with ideas, expertise and initiative. You will join an international organisation with strong brands, skilled colleagues, and opportunities to learn, grow, and develop throughout your career.

We value diversity and encourage all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of gender, age, background, or abilities. If you are motivated and have relevant experience, we welcome your application - even if you don't meet every requirement. If you need any adjustments or support during the recruitment process, please let us know.
Location and expected travel: The position can be based in Bankeryd, Sweden, or Bromsgrove, UK. International travel is expected as part of the role to support collaboration with colleagues, suppliers and manufacturing sites.
Application Deadline: December 13, 2026. We encourage candidates to apply before the current deadline, although the deadline may be extended if required.
Contact Information: If you have any questions regarding the role, you are welcome to contact: Ursula Bjecker, HRPB, ursula.bjercke@orkla.no

Klättermusen is looking for a Design Operations Manager
Since 1975 Klättermusen has been a pioneer in making refined Scandinavian Mountaineering Equipment. The designs combine utility and extreme durability, always with consideration of the environment in mind. Klättermusen supports and inspire outdoor enthusiasts through unforgiving weather conditions and unpredictable terrains. Rigorously tested in real-world conditions, the equipment embodies Klättermusen’s commitment to creating the best and most sustainable equipment available.
Klättermusen is looking for someone to lead the people, planning and operational performance of our Åre Design team. This senior role combines people leadership, commercial awareness, operational discipline and an understanding of product development. Working closely with the Head of Design, Design & Development leaders, Commercial, Production & Sourcing and our Shanghai colleagues, you will ensure that the Design organization has the clarity, capacity and structure to deliver strong products and support continued growth. At Klättermusen, Design connects product, function, problem-solving and brand development, and this role enables creativity, accountability and execution to work together. As Design Operations Manager, you will have personnel responsibility for the Åre Design team and lead planning, prioritisation and execution across seasons. You will oversee team performance, capacity, development planning and the Design & Development operating process, working closely with the Head of Design and functional leaders on strategic and product priorities. You will also partner with the Commercial Team to translate business and market needs into realistic, well-resourced development plans.
Key Responsibilities

Lead and develop the Åre Design team, including goals, coaching, performance, development and day-to-day people management.

Build a high-performing culture with clear expectations, accountability and strong individual development.

Own capacity planning, workload allocation and seasonal team planning.

Translate product and commercial priorities into clear development plans with realistic timelines and ownership.

Own and continuously improve the Design & Development operating process from approved brief through production handover.

Maintain seasonal calendars, milestones, decision gates, review cadence and escalation routes.

Identify risks, bottlenecks and resource constraints early and drive resolution across functions.

Work closely with the Commercial Team to align market needs, business priorities and development capacity.

Work with the Shanghai Design Operations Manager to align plans, sample calendars, reporting and ways of working across locations.

Strengthen collaboration across Design, Product Development, Pattern, Materials, Quality, Production & Sourcing and Commercial.

Support the Head of Design and functional leaders by taking ownership of people management, operational follow-up and organizational coordination.

Experience & Skills
We are looking for an experienced leader who understands how to build strong teams and deliver in a complex product environment.
You are comfortable operating across people, product, process and business priorities. You can move between strategic discussions and practical execution, create clarity in complex situations and make strong recommendations when trade-offs are required.

7+ years of relevant experience in technical apparel, outdoor product, design, product development, design operations or product programme leadership.

Proven experience leading and developing teams.

Strong understanding of end-to-end product development.

Experience with capacity planning, resource allocation and seasonal operating models.

Experience working closely with commercial teams.

Strong cross-functional and international collaboration skills.

Good understanding of technical packs, patterns, BOMs, PLM, sampling, fit, testing and production handover.

Professional English.

What Klättermusen offers

A forward-thinking design environment in a global outdoor brand

A role centered on innovation, exploration, and sustainable product development

Close collaboration with international production, sourcing teams, and testing environments

Opportunities for creative impact and professional growth

A workplace immersed in the outdoors — Åre is both our home and our testing ground

Work aligned with our guiding philosophy: “Maximum safety for you, minimum impact on nature.”

Klättermusen offers an exciting and rewarding work environment where your experience and passion are encouraged and supported. If you're ready to take the next step in your career and be part of our growing community, apply now and become part of the Klättermusen family!

The position is a full time position based in Åre. Welcome to apply by 2026-12-31.

We only accept applications through this channel. Your application will be stored in our database, and we will contact you if a suitable position becomes available. Applications will be handled on an ongoing basis.

The opportunity
At Hitachi Energy’s plant in Figeholm, we are looking for a Work Environment Engineer or HSE Specialist with an interest in fire protection, explosion risks, and chemical safety. In Figeholm, we manufacture cellulose-based insulation materials for the transformer industry. You will work in a technologically advanced manufacturing environment where safety considerations are closely linked to production, maintenance, chemical handling, and investment projects.
The role has a clear specialist focus, but you do not need to be an expert in all areas from day one. We are looking for someone with a solid foundation in occupational health and safety, risk management, or a related field, and a desire to further develop expertise in fire safety, explosion protection, and chemical safety. You will be part of the plant’s Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) function. Together with managers, employees, and technical specialists, you will identify risks and develop solutions that both meet regulatory requirements and support day-to-day operations. The role combines hands-on and strategic work. You will spend time on the production floor, lead risk assessments, and contribute specialist expertise to projects, process improvements, and operational changes.
How you’ll make an impact
Lead and support risk assessments related to occupational health and safety, fire protection, explosion risks, and chemical management.
Develop and strengthen the plant’s fire prevention and fire protection programs.
Support compliance and risk management activities related to flammable goods and explosive atmospheres (ATEX).
Support the safe handling, storage, and risk assessment of chemical products.
Translate legal requirements and Hitachi Energy’s HSE standards into practical procedures and ways of working.
Participate in incident investigations and follow up on corrective and preventive actions.
Provide HSE expertise in investment projects, engineering activities, and operational changes.
Conduct audits, inspections, and follow-up activities, contributing to continuous improvement initiatives.

Your background
Relevant university degree in occupational health and safety, safety engineering, fire protection, chemistry, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
Experience in occupational health and safety, risk management, or industrial safety within a manufacturing or industrial environment.
Experience conducting and documenting risk assessments.
Ability to translate technical and regulatory requirements into practical solutions and operational improvements.
Strong collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with production teams, technical specialists, and management.
You are confident in identifying risks and challenging existing ways of working when necessary. At the same time, you are solution-oriented and committed to developing improvements in close cooperation with the people who operate and support the business.
Strong knowledge of Quality Management Systems and relevant ISO standards.
Experience investigating and managing customer complaints, non-conformities, and quality-related issues.
Proven experience in root cause analysis and structured problem-solving methodologies.
Knowledge of Lean Six Sigma principles and continuous improvement practices.
Strong analytical skills combined with a structured and systematic approach to work.
Excellent communication skills in Swedish and English, both written and spoken.

Your New Role 
Our client, an international industrial group, is looking for a Compensation & Benefits Specialist to strengthen how its Group R&D organization manages pay and benefits and to bring C&B expertise to organizational design and grading initiatives.
In this role, you’ll help leaders understand how organizational changes affect pay, benefits and employment conditions across countries. Working primarily with stakeholders in Sweden and Germany, you’ll identify where practices can be aligned and develop shared principles for areas where local differences need to be managed. You’ll take ownership of ongoing initiatives and turn your analysis into clear options and recommendations for decision-makers.
What you’ll do

Lead the Group R&D Compensation & Benefits portfolio by setting priorities, clarifying ownership, tracking progress and reporting to management.

Represent Group R&D HR in strategic C&B forums and coordinate across Group HR, brand representatives, HR Business Partners and service providers.

Lead preparations for EU pay transparency requirements in Sweden and Germany by defining local delivery models, data needs and responsibilities, including how service providers will contribute.

Support the design and implementation of FY2027 compensation and incentive structures through analysis, recommendations and stakeholder coordination.

Map salary structures, incentives, benefits, employment conditions and annual C&B processes across R&D locations. Assess how they align with the common job architecture and grading framework and recommend ways to address significant differences.

Clarify how C&B services are delivered, including service-level agreements, provider requirements, data and benchmarking requests, and documentation for handover.

Advise on strategic organizational design and grading projects and assess how proposed changes will affect related HR processes.

Company Presentation
Our client is a global leader in the automotive industry, with operations in 100 countries. At their headquarter, they work on developing sustainable transport systems – mobility solutions that benefit businesses, society, and the environment. Here, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute your innovation and technical expertise to projects shaping the future of transportation, in an organization where collaboration, growth, and sustainability are key.
Good to Know
Scope of employment: Full-time, 100% Type of contract: Fixed-term employment as a consultant via JobBusters. Working model: Södertälje, with hybrid work and an expectation of 2-3 days per week in the office. Office days are agreed within the team. Start date: As agreed End date: 2027-07-09, with the possibility of extension Other information: Occasional travel between Sweden and Germany. In your application: Please ensure that your CV clearly demonstrates how you meet the qualifications required by the client.
To succeed in this role, you will need: 
A university degree or equivalent education in Human Resources, Business Administration, Economics or a related field.

Several years of relevant experience in Compensation & Benefits and organizational design within an international organization.

An understanding of grading methodologies and solid knowledge of fixed and variable pay, bonus and incentive eligibility, benefits and salary bands.

Experience working with HR Business Partners, service providers and Group functions in a matrix organization.

Strong analytical and strategic thinking skills, with advanced Excel and PowerPoint skills.

Strong communication skills in English. Proficiency in German, Swedish or Portuguese is a plus.

Meritorious: Certification in a recognized grading methodology or a project management qualification such as PMP, PRINCE2 or IPMA.

Meritorious: Knowledge of German collective agreements and Swedish compensation practices.

Meritorious: Experience designing or implementing job architecture, including job families, levels and career paths.

Meritorious: Experience with SAP SuccessFactors or a similar HR system.

Meritorious: Experience in a multi-brand, automotive or industrial environment.

What we Offer
Secure employment with a collective bargaining agreement, insurance coverage and occupational pension

Wellness allowance and employee discounts and offers via Benifex (e.g., health, leisure, transport and healthcare)

Flex pension and access to the Lifeplan pension advisory service

Additional compensation during parental leave

Occupational health services

Long-term assignments and a dedicated Consultant Manager for personal support

Opportunities to build valuable experience, expand your network and grow your future career
